newsitem.title: USA: Shell says Mars field "gradually" coming back.
newsitem.headline: Shell says Mars field "gradually" coming back.

text.p: Shell Oil Co said Tuesday that its Mars field in the deepwater sector of the Gulf of Mexico was gradually coming back up after an electrical problem forced production to shut down at the weekend.
"Mars went down Friday afternoon as the result of a problem with one of the electrical generating engines which provides power for the platform," said a Shell spokesperson.
Production began to come back up late Sunday/early Monday and is gradually rising back to the level seen before the outage, which was around 86,000 barrels per day (bpd), the spokesperson said.

The Mars field, located in nearly 3,000 feet of water about 130 miles southeast of New Orleans, produces medium-sour crude, with 31 degrees API (American Petroleum Institute) gravity rating, two percent sulphur and moderate metals content.
The crude is marketed via a three-million-barrel cavern in Louisiana, from where it feeds any of five major interconnecting pipelines to the national refining market.

Traders said the outage coincided with a rise in the relative price of sour crude in the Gulf. Marker West Texas Sour/Midland was up around 20 cents at around $2.10/$2.20 below West Texas Intermediate/Cushing compared with the end of last week.
Traders also noted that the closure of Mexico's main crude exporting ports over the past four days due to weather conditions is a contributing factor.
